summary_html: Federal transparency statutes—**FOIA** and **Sunshine Act**—require disclosure of government data. Project Milk Carton promotes FOIA requests and public dashboards for child-welfare records.
authority_html:

- **Government in the Sunshine Act (5 U.S.C. § 552b)** — open-meeting requirements

key_cases.case_name: Providence Journal Co. v. Rhode Island Department of Public Safety
key_cases.holding: Denial of the newspaper's Access to Public Records Act request for state police investigative records was affirmed because the subject's substantial privacy interest outweighed the asserted public interest, and a bare assertion of possible government impropriety does not compel disclosure.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling Rhode Island authority on the privacy exemption that most often blocks release of child-welfare-adjacent investigative records.
key_cases.quote: Pursuant to the APRA, records need not be disclosed where such disclosure could create an unwarranted invasion of privacy

key_cases.case_name: Pontarelli v. Rhode Island Department of Elementary & Secondary Education
key_cases.holding: The requested records fell within an APRA exception and were not public records, so the agency's denial was upheld; separately, any reason not stated in the denial is deemed waived absent good cause.
key_cases.relevance: The waiver rule under § 38-2-7(a) is the practical lever a requester has: reasons omitted from the denial letter are generally forfeited.
key_cases.quote: we hold without hesitation that the records Pontarelli requested are not public records for the purposes of APRA

key_cases.holding: Certiorari was denied to a clinical social worker resisting a grand jury subpoena for counseling records, because § 5-37.3-6.1 requires that the patient receive notice and an opportunity to be heard before process issues and the confidentiality questions can be fully litigated in the Superior Court.
key_cases.relevance: Any transparency request touching health care communications must accommodate the individual's right to notice and to contest disclosure.
key_cases.quote: Glatter's patient also must be afforded notice and an opportunity to be heard before process may issue for any confidential health care information.

key_cases.case_name: Direct Action for Rights & Equality v. Gannon
key_cases.holding: The 1998 APRA amendments applied to the pending action, so attorneys' fees ran from the filing of the complaint and no knowing and willful violation had to be shown to award them, while redaction of complainants' Social Security numbers and officers' badge numbers was properly allowed.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes both the pro-disclosure baseline and its practical limit, holding that unique personal identifiers may be redacted from otherwise releasable investigative records.
key_cases.quote: the underlying policy of the APRA is the promotion of the free flow and disclosure of information to the public
